# Isolated production worker

Run `npx tsx worker/index.ts --input /job/input.json --workspace /job`. Node 24.x, FFmpeg/FFprobe, Python 3, Poppler `pdftotext`, and Playwright Chromium are required. Python runs in explicit UTF-8 mode for portable plan validation. The web orchestrator supplies approved provider secrets to the isolated process, never the input file. Set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (or `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY`/`VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN`), `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`, `WORKER_CALLBACK_URL` (the job checkpoint URL), and the scoped `PIPELINE_CALLBACK_TOKEN`. `ANTHROPIC_MODEL`, `AI_GATEWAY_MODEL`, `ELEVENLABS_MUSIC_MODEL`, `PYTHON_PATH`, `FFMPEG_PATH`, `FFPROBE_PATH` and `VIDEO_STUDIO_SKILL_PATH` are optional runtime settings.

`WorkerInput` in `types.ts` is the server-to-worker contract. Private input/resume URLs are fetched with the callback bearer token only when their origin exactly matches the callback origin. Arbitrary destinations and every browser resource are DNS-validated, connection-pinned, redirect-validated and byte-limited. Reference links must directly return a video file. Social-page downloads and authentication bypasses are unsupported and produce an actionable input error.

The worker checkpoints artifacts to private object storage before recording completion. `POST artifact` with `{operation:"prepare",path,size,contentType,sha256}` returns `{clientToken,pathname,grant}`; the worker uploads directly to Blob with the scoped token, then commits `{operation:"complete",path,url,grant}`. `POST checkpoint` persists `{status,checkpoint}`, `{status:"ready",result}`, or `{status,error}`. Large videos never pass through a web function's request body.

Paid audio generation is reserved durably before the external request. Bytes are durably uploaded before that reservation is marked completed. Retries reuse a valid hashed output. Documented ElevenLabs rate-limit rejections allow at most three requests per logical audio asset, including the initial request. Each attempt and rejection is checkpointed; retries honor `Retry-After`, use bounded backoff, and remain inside the original job deadline. Credit and access failures stop with specific guidance. An interrupted or ambiguous reservation fails closed with `audio_payment_uncertain`; an operator must recover the external result or explicitly resolve the reservation. Legacy reservations remain unresolved unless verified by an operator. Model/audio/ASR usage and provider request IDs are recorded. Actual monetary cost is nullable until billing reconciliation, never fabricated from unverified estimates.

Direct Anthropic requests first use the free token-count endpoint with the same model, system message and complete input. The count is an estimate: the worker reserves 15% plus 1,024 tokens above it, records request hashes and the reservation before generation, and reconciles actual usage afterward. Gateway requests or an unavailable/invalid counter retain the conservative byte/pixel estimate. A usage overrun or unresolved prior model reservation stops further automatic provider calls; budgets are never enlarged to make a review pass. See [Anthropic's token-counting documentation](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/token-counting).

The pinned unified skill owns the workflow. The runtime hashes its loaded chapters and refuses to resume under a changed skill/runtime. Production proceeds through source capture, structured research, on-screen scripting, trusted HTML motion composition, audio and final quality review. Research facts retain exact source quotes and visual IDs; every script beat binds to those facts. The research and script stages are reserved before paid calls and completed only after hashed artifacts are persisted. An interrupted or altered stage fails closed instead of repeating paid work.

`reference-style.json` records the reusable motion grammar derived from all 660 frames of the supplied reference: problem, brand, real product proof, features, a supported offer or further proof, then CTA. Scripts usually aim for six scenes and 20–28 seconds, extending when reading or intact source speech requires it. Reference imagery, brand copy, pricing, voices and soundtrack are never reused. Offer cards require explicit pricing or free-offer evidence for every card. Other cards are explanatory product facts, not fabricated application interfaces or demonstrated results.

Every plan has frame-exact contiguous scenes and supporting literal source quotes. New compositions render escaped source copy into trusted local HTML and a paused GSAP timeline exported by the pinned Hyperframes runtime. Models cannot supply executable HTML or JavaScript. Local licensed Geist typography, contained real screenshots/recordings, restrained type and card entrances, and light/dark scene transitions follow the reference profile. Editable composition files and source hashes are retained. The FFmpeg audio mixer produces full-HD H.264/AAC with instrumental music and selective SFX. Speech-bearing product recordings are used whole or rejected; music is ducked below them. No TTS or generated voiceover endpoint exists.

URL capture keeps page screenshots for context and may additionally retrieve complete, publicly linked product raster images. The extractor filters logos, portraits and unsuitable dimensions, records original-image hashes/provenance, and uses the same 55 MB capture budget. It accepts at most four originals in six attempts, with a 24 MB local byte allowance and a 20-second scheduling cutoff; in-flight requests retain the existing inactivity timeout and whole-worker ceiling. These are public-page images, never represented as authenticated application captures. Analysis uses smaller previews while rendering retains the complete normalized source.

Research may follow up to two visible, observed same-origin pricing/product/features links. Homepage and follow-ups share the 55 MB/500-request capture allowance; extra pages have a 30-second scheduling window, 12-second navigation ceilings, at most 7,500 text characters and one actual screenshot each. Aggregate source text is bounded at 45,000 characters. Query, credential, account, authentication, action, download and API destinations are excluded before every redirect request. `analysis/research-sources.json` records provenance and optional capture failures. An unavailable linked page leaves usable homepage evidence intact.

Delivery requires full-file decode and metadata validation, timeline/source bounds, DOM layout inspection, Claude review of actual decoded scene/hold/seam frames, source-grounded claims, reference-source exclusion, actual loudness/true-peak measurement, and final Scribe speech/audio-event analysis. The QC record describes performed checks and explicitly does not claim human listening. Up to two targeted repairs are allowed. Failure remains `needs_review`; no fallback/demo output is published. Internal sources, scene HTML, composition, plan, storyboard, draft, usage, reviews, final and poster are retained by the host's retention policy.

Repairs reserve their allowance in `analysis/repair-ledger.json` before any paid repair call. Retries restore the consumed count and verify the last applied plan hash; an unresolved reservation fails closed for operator review. The worker also honors dispatch's absolute `deadlineAt`, using the smaller remaining job time or attempt allowance. Retries cannot reset either repair or total execution limits. Non-rendered summary/purpose/reference-technique notes are bounded deterministically while raw provider responses remain retained; visible copy, source grounding and timeline validation are unchanged.

Validation commands: `npm test`, `npm run typecheck`. A real paid end-to-end acceptance run requires configured providers and the durable artifact service. Unit tests alone do not certify generated video quality.

`node --env-file=.env.local --import tsx scripts/acceptance-local.ts --run-paid --url https://example.com --workspace .local/acceptance-example` exercises the exported pipeline locally with actual providers and verified filesystem checkpoints. `--fixture .local/acceptance-fixtures/submission-fixture.json` can replace `--url` for an explicitly authorized PRD/reference acceptance. The fixture adapter verifies exact manifest hashes, sizes and confined paths; only this local runner supplies its programmatic input-reader dependency. The production CLI and API always use the normal public-network and authenticated-upload reader. Local success does not prove production uploads, queue execution, private storage or owner access. The operator must have authorization for the supplied source material to be analyzed by the configured external providers. `--run-paid` is a deliberate execution flag, not a substitute for that authorization.

The local runner preserves raw responses and aggregate provider usage across explicit recovery. Saved-review recovery uses actual retained findings to request a repair and performs fresh complete QC afterward; it never promotes an earlier partial review to a passed check. Once a retained-review repair is reserved, further resume of that recovery folder is prohibited so its consumed repair allowance cannot reset. Claude visual review compares actual output frames with original source previews, and reference acceptance requires both a performed comparison and an explicit successful style-adoption assessment.

`npx tsx worker/smoke-motion.ts --out .local/motion-smoke --format 16:9` renders a six-beat synthetic HTML motion film with test-tone audio, full-file decode, exact frame counts and inspection frames. This fixture cannot invoke delivery or providers and does not certify generated product content. After `node scripts/bundle-worker.mjs`, `worker/smoke-sandbox.ts` runs that film in all three ratios in the configured Linux snapshot and retrieves the MP4s, contact sheets and render reports. A worker snapshot must contain the pinned Playwright, Hyperframes and GSAP dependencies plus Chromium, FFmpeg, Python and Poppler; `scripts/create-worker-snapshot.ts` prepares it. Provider-backed end-to-end acceptance remains a separate check.

# Specialized constructions in the shared timeline

These recipes are not preinstalled engines. Check dependencies and render intermediates first.

## Data/decks/infographics

Use supplied data and explicit field/unit mapping. Design settled frame first. Declare scale, use zero baseline for bars unless truncation is obvious, stable IDs for rank interpolation. Round display apart from actual values; exact final counters match source. Reveal headline → primary statistic/chart → explanation → source. Inspect start/mid/final. Narration sets deck holds. Recompute per aspect.

## Diagrams/maps/math

Nodes precede edges; label relationships, anchor connectors, reveal arrows without occlusion. Whiteboard paths draw in teaching order. Isometric uses consistent geometry/camera. Maps require real coordinates/projection/boundaries, consistent data projection, dataset/tile attribution. Camera motion expresses a supported relationship. Math shows correct symbols and meaningful steps. Installed Manim may prerender a segment; a browser mock is not a Manim render.

## Web to video

GSAP/SVG/Lottie/React motion patterns supply stagger/reveal/morph/spatial behavior. Convert scroll/hover/click into authored functions of frame. Canvas redraw receives t=frame/fps. No live input, network timing, wall clock, or unseeded randomness. Bundle local dependencies; verify seeking. A separately requested web artifact preserves accessibility/reduced-motion independently of exported video.

## 3D/illustration/creative code

Real product models/materials matter for fidelity. WebGL/Blender require locked camera/lights/fps/seed/quality/local assets. Smoke-render before whole sequence. No silent 3D/live-action downgrade to 2D. Shader effects must seek deterministically.

Zero-asset canvas layers background → silhouette → detail → accents with fixed seed. Painted/crayon/cel/pixel/paper/line treatments share storyboard/time. Pixel art uses integer scaling, paper-cut consistent edge/shadow/light, whiteboard explanatory strokes. Validate source character/product consistency. Code-made music needs offline rendered WAV; real-time Web Audio callbacks do not automatically survive export.

One job directory:
```

assets/                  originals, screenshots, generated intermediates
analysis/                probes, frames, transcripts, style.json
plan.json                authoritative asset/timeline contract

renders/                 draft.mp4, final.mp4, poster.jpg

```

`job.json` includes job_id, request, mode edit/create, inputs, reference, output preferences, provider configuration, budgets, and automatic (true for upload-to-edit SaaS). Never store keys here.

Use integer timeline frames at integer fps (24/25/30/50/60 in v1). Source offsets are seconds. Frame intervals are half-open [start,end). Base scenes cover output contiguously. Extra graphics/captions/audio/transition layers do not redefine base duration. Source consumption = duration_frames / fps × playback_rate. Crossfades need real handles or explicitly planned held frames. Effects describe overlap, stacking, and implementation. FFmpeg roughcut refuses effects.

See `../assets/plan-example.json`. Required fields:
- version: 1; job_id; mode edit/create; renderer hyperframes/ffmpeg/remotion.
- output: width, height, fps, duration_frames.
- assets: id, path, kind video/image/audio, usage output/reference, rights; measured duration_seconds/has_audio when applicable.
- scenes: id, start_frame, duration_frames, asset_id, source_in_seconds, playback_rate, preserve_audio, fit contain/cover, purpose, reference_technique, effects.
- captions: text, start_frame, end_frame; optional words/style.
- audio: asset_id, start_frame, duration_frames, source_in_seconds, playback_rate, gain_db, role.

Assets are local files relative to plan.json or absolute within the job directory. Arbitrary remote URLs never enter the renderer. Reference assets are analysis-only and cannot be used as output media. Materialize generated graphics as image/video before validation. The helper independently probes sources rather than trusting manifest duration/audio claims.

Preserve-audio scenes imply source audio; do not duplicate them in audio. Map actual ASR/TTS word times through kept intervals: for source word time w, kept source start s, timeline start T, rate r, output time = T + (w-s)/r. Clip words to retained intervals, then listen around crossing edits. Captions are on final timeline, not raw-source time.

qc.json: status passed/needs_review/failed; technical, visual, speech/caption, reference checks; findings, repairs, evidence. Unperformed checks are not_checked. result.json: job_id, status (completed/needs_review/needs_input/failed/cancelled), outputs/storage keys, assumptions, unmet requests, observed costs, renderer/model/skill versions, QC path.

# Motion, typography, seams, captions

Define one system: canvas, safe rectangles, local fonts, hierarchy, palette, spacing, strokes, corner radii, motion vocabulary. Reuse tokens. Inspect actual brand/reference; product content is better than unrelated decorative cards. Actual fonts avoid changing text metrics.

Motion communicates cause, attention, or state: position/scale/opacity/mask/camera/drawing. Avoid constant idle wobble. Stillness helps accent a reveal. Fixed values and seeded randomness reproduce arbitrary seeks.

## Recipes on one clock

- Kinetic type: semantic units; quick stagger then reading hold; emphasize only important words.
- UI: real screenshot → cursor to actual control → click → real result → useful focal zoom.
- Lower third: accurate identity/title; hold then exit without hiding face/captions.
- Countdown/counter: derive value from frame, tabular numerals, exact endpoint, real deadline.
- Logo: preserve proportions/clear space and recognition.
- SVG/whiteboard: explanatory path order; nodes before connector edges.
- Comparison: equal scale, clear labels, shared anchor for match-cut when useful.
- Photo: deliberately varied focal paths; retain faces/objects.

## Seams

A continuous move can carry axis, direction, and perceived speed across a cut. Growing scale continues a push; shrinking continues a pull. Cut mid-motion only if content remains readable. Hard footage cuts are valid; do not impose continuous camera motion on all edits.

Choose cut/match-cut/slide/zoom-through/crossfade/rack-focus for content, usually one dominant family. Plan overlap, stacking, source handles, audio. An opaque stage prevents opacity-dip flashes. Inspect before/during/after each seam. A transition never hides the payoff or destroys speech.

## Captions

Use real ASR/TTS times mapped to final edit. Group short semantic phrases, sensible line breaks, typically up to two lines as a starting point. Word highlights require actual word timing. Measure actual rendered text, constrain width, inspect contrast/backplate and faces/platform controls. Safe areas vary; use configured platform overlays or conservative margins and inspect every aspect.

Check first/last words, names/numbers, sentence ends, overlaps, and edit boundaries. SRT is plain timed text; animated words live in the composition. Real-time CSS animations/timers/autoplay/requestAnimationFrame cannot drive export. Convert web interaction into the seekable frame clock. Hyperframes uses one paused GSAP timeline per composition and runtime-owned clip visibility.

# Reference analysis and footage editing

## Build evidence

Obtain actual reference media through the configured ingestion adapter. IG/TT downloads are not guaranteed; reference upload is the fallback. Record screen UI/black bars and crop analysis appropriately. No successful metadata lookup means you watched the video.

Probe reference and raw footage. Sample regular frames and candidate cuts; listen to audio. Proxies support analysis; final rendering uses originals. `video_tool.py inspect` produces probe.json, a contact sheet, and heuristic silence/cut logs. Scene detector outputs are candidates, not semantic edits.

Transcribe speech with actual word timestamps using configured ASR. Index source ranges, complete thoughts, take quality, visible actions, subjects, framing, and useful B-roll. Do not infer words from stills or claim brightness heuristics are face tracking.

Write style.json with canvas, shot timing distribution, opening device, narrative functions, crop/subject placement, typography, caption grouping, palette, motion families, transitions, and sound accents. Each observation includes source time and measured/estimated status. Approximate uncertain font/BPM measurements honestly.

## Construct the edit

Keep best complete takes. Remove false starts/dead air where meaning survives. Silence can be intentional. Preserve negations, caveats, contractions, names, numbers, and breathing needed for natural speech. Optional crutch-word removal is checked by listening.

Map raw material to reference FUNCTIONS: hook, evidence, explanation, reaction, payoff. Apply pacing/visual grammar to the user's content. Reordering cannot create a different claim. Do not append a product CTA to editorial footage because a promo recipe includes one.

Inspect subjects across time for vertical cropping. Use a stable safe crop, an available tracker, or fit/letterbox. Check eyes, hands, demo object, speaker changes. Normalize rotation/VFR when the runtime requires it. Do not promise automatic face tracking without an actual tracker.

Plan cut/crop/zoom/hold/freeze/overlay/caption/B-roll/transition/speed explicitly. Source speech speed stays unchanged unless asked; synchronize audio and remap words if changed. Graphics emphasize specific meaning. B-roll must match the topic and can retain original speech underneath.

## Compare to reference

Review opening, representative shot lengths, cuts, caption density/placement, palette, motion direction/energy, and sound balance. Explain deviations caused by footage. No fabricated exact-match score. Transfer craft rather than reference characters, claims, soundtrack, or brand. Requested reproduction still uses authorized assets under the ingestion policy.

Start with viewer, one message, intended outcome, available evidence. Default choices fill missing details without a long interview. A finished-video request authorizes planning and rendering; genuinely missing essentials go to needs_input.

## Product URL / PRD / screenshots

Capture actual UI and brand assets. Distinguish shipped features from planned PRD items. Record supported claims. Select a central flow: entry → meaningful action → visible result. Show the actual product delivering it. Use real screenshots for controlled staging, recordings when the interaction proves the claim.

A starting 15–25 second arc is hook → reveal → 2–3 demonstrated benefits → outcome/CTA. Adapt duration to message. Make the product recognizable early. Never invent testimonials, metrics, urgency, discounts, capabilities, or interfaces.

Storyboard exact duration, purpose, source, text, composition, attention target, entry/hold/exit, transition, sound. “Cinematic” is not a scene spec. | Demo | Setup → action → result; actual UI, deliberate cursor, focal zoom | Actual controls/results |
| Launch/teaser | Hook → reveal → feature montage → outcome | Brand/reveal timing |
| Performance ad | One promise, supported evidence, one CTA | Message matches destination |
| Testimonial | Supplied verbatim quote, exact author/rating | Attribution/text |
| Offer/sale | Product, accurate offer, terms/code, CTA | Price and real deadlines |
| Explainer | Question → mechanism → example → takeaway | One idea per beat |
| Deck | Rebuild slides, narration determines holds | Values/build order |
| Photo slideshow | Subject-aware fit, varied restrained pan/zoom | Faces/framing |
| Podcast/audiogram | Speech-first highlights, actual waveform, captions | Quote/timing |
| Text story | Source-backed or clearly fictional bubbles | Reading time/attribution |
| Wrapped/recap | Meaningful stat/highlight progression | Units/exact values |
| PR/release | Real diff → behavior consequence → before/after | Grounded change |
